condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

Target 1: Target 1.1.2 National survey of consumption of HFCs and other alternative cooling agents (natural cooling agents) and their uses undertaken for government to consider the impact of the Kigali Amendment on phase out of HFCs. Target 1.2.1 Two proposals to upgrade legislation prepared and provided to the National Partners consideration, and accepted Target 1.3.1 Central Customs Laboratory provided with, at least, ten (10) samples of 5 types of refrigerant’ standards for calibrating their gas chromatographs and updating software. Target 1.3.2: At least 50 importers and environmental inspectors, including, at least, 30% women, trained, and improved their knowledge on the use of a newly introduced electronic systems of declaring ODS/ODS alternatives import/export. Target 1.3.3: Extended capacity of the State Customs Committee of centralized storage of seized smuggled ODS/ODS alternatives is available
Target 2: Target 2.1.1 Established Six (6) new (4 recycling and 2 reclaim) and upgraded six (6) operating (5 recycling and 1 reclaim) centers Target 2.1.4 100 public and private enterprises of the RAC sector benefited from project interventions in terms of servicing tools supplies Target 2.1.5 Six newly established and six existing HCFC re-use centers able to develop technical/business plans to ensure sustainability of operations over longer term Target 2.2.1 One demonstration project implemented in public facilities/ commercial applications/ training centers Target 2.2.4 5 refrigeration technicians that improved knowledge to assemble, install, operate and maintain zero-ODS low GWP Target 2.2.5 One thematic discussion with RAC technologies users on application of zero-ODS low GWP alternative technologies conducted Target 2.4.1 Three vocational training centers established and equipped in the regions of Uzbekistan Target 2.4.4 One networking and experience exchange with foreign counterparts from the CEIT region conducted
Target 3: Target 3.1.1 Four information materials developed Target 3.1.2 1 awareness raising activity implemented Target 3.2.3 A comprehensive resource mobilization strategy developed
Target 4: Target 4.1.1 Two start-up businesses of women supported that ensured higher job placement rate for women studying RAC sector related business Target 4.1.3 A comprehensive survey conducted, and its results are available Target 4.2 a) Regular monitoring and evaluation of the project activities and results conducted and presented during Project Board meetings, which organized twice in a year and serve as guidance to project’s implementation plan. Target 4.1.b) KM products prepared throughout the project implementation on its achievements to inform wider audience in the country and in regional and international meetings

Target 1.1.2: Data on sectoral use of ODS and ODS alternatives collected for the period of 2010-2020 (first half); Feasibility and implications study of ratification of Kigali amendment for the Republic of Uzbekistan conducted
Target 1.2.1: Inputs to drafting resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers on “National program on Complete ODS phase-out” and the resolutions roadmap provided and included: 1. Establishment of the National Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning (RAC) Association to support the government in the development of relevant legislation, industry wide data gathering for effective decision-making and implementation of RAC relevant policies and state programmes; 2. Inclusion of four project activities to the Roadmap of the Resolution: (i) Support in enhancement of national legislation, including assessment of the Kigali Amendments ratification; capacity building of Customs and enforcement officers on the control of HCFCs and ODS alternatives during import/export; (ii) Strengthening the HCFC re-use system and implementation of demonstration projects on HCFC replacement with ODS-free/low GWP alternatives; (iii) Information exchange within the industries and awareness raising among stakeholders; (iv) Attracting women to RAC sector through education, new business skills. The draft Resolution, along with the roadmap, is currently under discussion at the President office.
Target 1.3.1: Staff of the Uzbek State Customs Laboratory learned on how to develop a sample standard for gas chromatograph calibration by several equipment which are available their Laboratory from the Istanbul Central Customs Laboratory colleagues within the study tour organized by project team. This avoided the need of sample standards procurement for calibration of gas chromatograph.
Target 1.3.2: 188 participants (8 females) trained in detection of ODS in export-import operations and on e-validation of the import of goods/cooling agents through newly introduced online platform Single Window within the online scientific/practical workshop conducted on 14 September 2020.
Target 1.3.3: Inputs provided to development of the Parties document with technical specifications of the equipment for establishment of the centralized storage of seized smuggled ODS/ODS alternatives developed with the State Customs Committee; corresponding procurement (forklift, pallet rackings, euro-pallets and repairing services) done, except forklift which delivery is scheduled for the end of December 2020.
Target 2.1.1: Technical documentation (ToR) for establishing of two (2) Reclaim and four (4) Recycle centers and additional equipment for existing one (1) Reclaim center and six (5) Recycle centers finalized; and equipment with tools procured; equipment and tools for temporary use will be transferred to the end-users by the end 2020.
Target 2.1.4: RAC equipment spare parts for one hundred (100) public and private enterprises procured; spare parts will be transferred to the end-users by the end 2020.
Target 2.1.5: 14 participants (one female) represented management and personnel of Recycle/Reclaim centers skilled to develop business plans through training within online workshops conducted in October 2020; Business plans aimed at ensuring sustainability of eleven recovery and recycling centers available.
Target 2.2.1: Technical documentation (contribution of parties with technical specification) for the demonstration project with LLC “Khiva Maishiy Texnika” on application of zero-ODS, low-GWP and energy efficient technology developed; Equipment and tools for the demonstration project with LLC “Khiva Maishiy Texnika” procured; and will be transferred for temporary use by the end-users by the end 2020.
Target 2.2.4: Training for users/operators after implementation of energy-efficient, zero-ODS and low-GWP technologies designed but postponed due to UN restrictions release for travels during COVID-19 pandemic.
Target 2.2.5: 7 representatives of RAC sector companies and independent experts participated in online technical/thematic discussions during February-April 2020. Relevant proposals for improvement of RAC sector collected and analyzed.
Target 2.4.1: Technical documentation (contribution of parties with technical specification of equipment) for establishing three training centers developed; Equipment and tools (except for CO2 Heat pump) procured and will be transferred for temporary use by the end-users by the end 2020.
Target 2.4.4: Sharing of experience on implementation of new Regional Project on Kigali Amendment and implementation of demo project on R290 split air-conditioners as well as on R290 monoblocs done (virtually) and technical documents shared with UNDP Tajikistan colleagues.
Target 3.1.1: Communication strategy 2020-24 developed; Two animation clips for kids and public audience developed in three languages (Uzbek, Russian and Karakalpak) with English subtitles; One infographics for kids produced; Three e-banners: contest announcement for celebration of World Ozone Day, contest for selection of demonstration projects and banner for World Ozone Day event produced; Four types of promo materials: powerbank, umbrealla, eco-bag and USB stick produced; 4000 kids’ poster printed for awareness raising campaign printed; diploma and certificates for the winners of the World Ozone Day contest printed;
Target 3.1.2: 192 participants (46 females) participated in 10-day online contest (in the form of quiz) on the occasion of the World Environment Day encouraging for action on the protection of the Ozone Layer; Online Contest in three categories devoted to World Ozone Day conducted and resulted in receipt of 22 poems, 28 videoclips and 18 articles; Media coverage of Uzbekistan participation in COP12/MOP32 done in November 2020; Media coverage of Project Board Meeting done on 3 December 2020.
Target 3.2.3: International expert for resource mobilization strategy recruited; a resource mobilization strategy for RAC sector will be completed by the end 2020.
Target 4.1.1 This activity was postponed to the next year due to COVID-19 related UN and local restrictions for people gathering and travel, as it is closely linked to a PR campaign and results of the gender survey/roadmap.
Target 4.1.3 Despite the pandemic restrictions on the collection of survey participants in person, the gender survey aimed at identification of barriers to attract women into the RAC sector conducted via telegram messenger: in total, 3233 participants from mahallas (849 women and 353 men), institutes/universities (297 women and 752 men), professional schools (333 women and 575 men) and the project’s partner RAC companies (9 women and 65 men) in all regions of Uzbekistan; and the survey’s findings formulated, recommendations on gender mainstreaming presented and developed RoadMap to attract women to RAC sector will be sent for government (State Committee for Ecology and Environmental Protection) consideration; developed recommendations and roadmap for gender mainstreaming in project activities will be implemented during project implementation.
Target 4.2 a) Regular online monitoring conducted, and results were presented during the Project Board meeting held on 3 December 2020; Data on use of ODS and their alternatives for the first, second and third quarters of 2020 collected from 100 private and public companies.
Target 4.1.b) Project results and relevant knowledge management products are carefully collected for wider dissemination.

Target 1 Target 1.2.2 The results of the analysis/review of the rules regarding the disposal and reuse of ODS, as well as the proper dismantling and disposal of equipment containing ODS, were submitted to the specialists of the State Committee for Ecology, and further development of proposals for improving national legislation.
Target 1.3.2 30 (4 women - 13%) environmental from 14 regions of Uzbekistan and 2 customs officials from State Customs Laboratory improved their knowledge on types of refrigerants in current import/export activities and knowledge on the use of an electronic systems of declaring ODS/ODS alternatives import/export in Uzbekistan during the summer school in August 2022.
Target 1.3.5 Network built with UNECE -joint case study developed on potential for improving energy efficiency in the refrigeration and air conditioning sector in Uzbekistan (2021-2022); - Shared experience with UNEP OzonAction CEIT Network in implementing Uzbekistan’s Program on phasing out ODS within ECA meeting (online) (January 2022); - Organized several meetings with representatives of “Artel” company – key player in manufacturing RAC equipment in Uzbekistan and Central Asia, on advantages of application of zero-ODS, low GWP alternative technologies and knowledge sharing on transition to green technology in RAC sector, particularly on split ACs (2021- 2022): (i) a meeting about the Kigali amendment and available HFC-free technologies for split air-conditioning equipment Artel produces and (ii) Artel’s technicians visit to Tashkent State Technical University to get acquainted with R290 split ACs and R744 heat pump.
Target 1.4 Conducted training - summer school (August 2022) for environmental and customs officials to develop professional skills in covering ozone issues, including speaking at public events.
Target 2 Target 2.1.2 2,471 kg of HCFCs have been recycled and 390 kg of HCFCs have been reclaimed based on collected data via report.o3.uz - this helps in further capacity strengthening for the national HCFC re-use system that will allow to dramatically reduce HCFC importations in line with Uzbekistans obligations under the Montreal Protocol.
Target 2.1.4 Collected information from all regions of Uzbekistan to update database and announce contest to select RAC companies for servicing tools supplies.
Target 2.2.1 In total four (4) demonstration projects are being implemented: one in public facility, three in commercial applications (two manufacturers of equipment and a warehouse/cold-room): - Demonstration project with LLC “Khiva Maishiy Texnika” on “Replacement of small-scale production commercial refrigeration line using HCFCs to zero-ODS and low-GWP technology on natural refrigerants – propane (R290) and/or isobutane (R600a)” is fully operational. - Based on experience of LLC “Khiva Maishiy Texnika”, the demonstration project with Family Enterprise “Albatros Service” has launched in test mode with the production of 2 display refrigerators on R290 in 2022. - Demonstration project with Jizzakh branch of the Republican Research Center for Emergency Medicine (RRCEM) on replacement of HCFC-based air-conditioning system with ozone-friendly, low GWP and energy-efficient technology has continued. The reconstructions works has started with estimate cost of 9 billion UZS (USD 834 thousand, UNORE December 2021) where replacement of the air-conditioning system is envisaged. After review of the applicable technologies, additional UZS 1 billion (about USD 96,000) requested to allocate for implementation of the demonstration project. Therefore, additional 1 billion UZS is mobilized from Jizzakh Regional State Administration (Khakimiyat) for implementation of the demonstration project, including transferred amount of 535 million UZS (about USD 48,000) to UNDP account in May 2022 for procurement of chillers, installation and commissioning works. The commissioning of centralized air-conditioning system of RRCEM is scheduled for Q1 of 2023. - The demonstration project with “??? Adolat Temir” LLC (Tashkent city) on “Replacement of refrigeration system in cold-room using HCFCs (R22) to energy efficient and ozone-friendly technologies with low global warming potential” has been launched.
Target 2.2.2 Awareness raising campaigns held on benefits of new technologies, supported to broaden project’s positive impacts and exploration of scale-up opportunities in partnership with other-than-GEF funding sources: - Jointly with the UNDP project “Towards Green Recovery in Uzbekistan” in cooperation with the farm “Seit Sharwa” (Takhtakupir district, Republic of Karakalpakstan) partnership agreement (“Contribution of parties”) for the demonstration project “Installation of energy efficient and ozone-friendly technologies with low global warming potential refrigeration system in cold-room for storage of dairy products” has been developed. Contracts for delivery of equipment (two monoblocs on R290) and installation are signed and refrigeration system was purchased and installed. - A case study on potential for improving energy efficiency in the refrigeration and air conditioning sector in Uzbekistan developed, published in cooperation with UNECE (USD 7,500 during August 2021 – February 2022) with involvement of 5 experts (1 women), and was presented at the International Scientific and Practical Conference.
Target 2.2.4 Conducted workshop for 32 technicians (2 women) including representatives of 11 Reclaim and Recycle centers and 2 Demonstration projects on advantages of application of zero-ODS, low-GWP alternative technologies in Khiva city (May 2022).
Target 2.2.5 Conducted a thematic meeting with participation of 20 participants (5 women) including representatives of “Artel” company, the largest RAC equipment producer in Uzbekistan and Central Asia, on advantages of application of zero-ODS, low-GWP alternative technologies and knowledge sharing on transition to green technology in RAC sector, particularly on household split ACs (April 2022).
Target 2.3.1 HCFC based equipment performance monitoring system system is installed in LLC JV UZ Dong Ju Paint Co (Andijan city, Andijan region). and the equipment is connected to the chiller of the company and constantly monitoring (in real-time mode) energy consumption and overall operation. The project is planning to analyze collected one-year data during the next year.
Target 2.4.3 260 technicians (48% women) trained through the launched web-site (www.e-learning.o3.uz) and skills are upgraded on best practices in refrigeration (RAC), including ozone-friendly and energy efficient technology with low GWP. - 273 technicians (9 women) from 9 regions trained onsite training programmes on best practices in refrigeration (RAC), including ozone-friendly and energy efficient technology with low GWP.
Target 2.4.4 Representatives of the Project shared experience with UNEP OzonAction CEIT Network in implementing Uzbekistan’s Program on phasing out ODS within ECA meeting (online) in January 2022 - Representatives of the Project learned experience with UNEP OzonAction CEIT Network in the topic “Czech Republic’s Montreal protocol experience and preparation of Kigali HFC implementation plans (KIPs)” within ECA meeting in Prague Czech Republic in September 2022.
Target 3 Target 3.1.1 - 194 social media posts and articles published at UNDP and partners’ media channels in 2022; - An online RAC training program for refrigeration technicians in Uzbek and Russian languages, is developed and launched at https://e-learning.o3.uz/ with possibility of issuing certificates on successful completion after online assessment; - Video interview “Women in technical professions in Uzbekistan” as a continuation of gender-mainstreaming series in RAC sector in Uzbek and Russian languages (April 2022); - “Ozone for life: unfolding the potential of women-technicians” to promote and strengthen role of women in technical sphere (March 2022).
Target 3.1.2 - World Earth Day: promotion of videoclip developed about women in the technical field, contributing to the introduction of green technologies to protect the environment and preserve the Earths ozone layer; - World Environment Day: Radio Q&A quiz at “Avtoradio” station and award ceremony at the event devoted to World Environment Day; - International Day for the Protection of the Ozone Layer: 35th Anniversary of the Montreal Protocol celebrated on High-level event in cooperation with TSTU. At the event: a)The winners of the contest among female students of TSTU for a one-year study grant were announced b) The winners of the international research paper contest were announced Collaboration with Ministry of Public Education: large outreach activities to 10,104 schools countrywide for conducting lessons on Ozone Layer importance, total of 1,793,491 pupils.
Target 3.2.1 UNDP project “Towards Green Recovery in Uzbekistan” for farm “Seit Sharwa” (Takhtakupir district, Republic of Karakalpakstan) as a donor is engaged in technical assistance and has allocated USD 33,049 (UNORE June 2022) for installation of energy efficient, ozone-friendly refrigeration system with low global warming potential for the cold-room of dairy products to increase application of advanced technologies in RAC sector.
Target 3.2.3 - Based on comprehensive resource mobilization strategy for RAC sector, financial resources are mobilized for development of the National Cooling Action Plan for Uzbekistan.. Two donors - Jizzakh Regional Khokimiyat and UNDP project “Towards Green Recovery in Uzbekistan” were involved to implement demonstration projects on energy-efficient, ozone-friendly and low-GWP technologies.
Target 3.2.4 During the reporting period, one (1) organization is engaged with the new financial mechanisms (public sector funding sources): Jizzakh Regional State Administration (Khakimiyat) allocated 1 billion UZS (about USD 89,206 – UNORE May 2022) for implementation of advanced RAC technology (energy-efficient, ozone-friendly and low-GWP) in Jizzakh branch of the Republican Research Center for Emergency Medicine showcasing that the Government/local authorities can allocate funds upon request for renovation of air-conditioning system in public buildings.
Target 4 Target 4.1.2 - Three women students were provided stipend scheme to study RAC in Tashkent State Technical University by the Evaluation Panel as the winners of the grant competition.
Target 4.1.4 A) 19 Partnership agreements were signed in 2022: - Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the State Committee for Ecology and UNDP has been signed (January 2022); - Letter of Agreement (LOA) and Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) were signed between UNDP and Tashkent State Technical University for provision of one-year scholarship for two women/girls students who study RAC in Tashkent State Technical University. - The State Committee has signed 16 agreements with project partner-companies (12 Reclaim/recycle centers and 4 Women startup companies). B) 4 joint activities with partners conducted: - with State Committee of the Republic of Uzbekistan for Ecology and Environmental Protection: - World Earth Day: promotion of videoclip developed about women in the technical field; - World Environment Day: Radio Q&A quiz at “Avtoradio” station; - with Tashkent State Technical University: - International Day for the Protection of the Ozone Layer: 35th Anniversary of the Montreal Protocol; - with Ministry of Public Education: - Outreach activities to 10,104 schools countrywide for conducting lessons on Ozone Layer importance.
Target 4.2 a) - Monitoring visits were carried out in 45 project partner companies in Ferghana, Andijan, Namangan, Khorezm, Bukhara and Navoi regions, including gender start-up companies – “Sovitish va konditsionerlash” LLC in Fergana region and “Zamin Madad Tayyorlov Savdo” LLC in Bukhara region and a pilot project to reduce HCFC leaks at “Uz-Dong Ju Paint Co” LLC in Andijan region. The results were presented during the 8th Project Board meeting held in November 2022; - Data on use of ODS and their alternatives for the first, second and third quarters of 2022 collected from 104 private and public companies.
Target 4.2 b) Project results and relevant knowledge management products were carefully collected for wider dissemination: - An online RAC training program for refrigeration technicians in Russian version of the online learning system https://e-learning.o3.uz/ was developed in Q3 of 2022 and is fully operational in Uzbek and Russian languages; - Video interview “Women in technical professions in Uzbekistan” as a continuation of gender-mainstreaming series in RAC sector in Uzbek and Russian languages was shot in April of 2022; - 194 social media posts and articles published at UNDP and partners’ media channels; - “Ozone for life: unfolding the potential of women-technicians” to promote and strengthen role of women in technical sphere (March 2022). - Updated (practical) training modules on practical side (educational methodological complexes, focus on case studies with the use of handed-over stands) were developed for (1) training of trainers and (2) advanced training of trainers in Russian and Uzbek languages.
